fatal_errors: The structural mediator and mechanism are imported from an unrelated Re-alloyed NbMoTaW/NbMoTaWRe irradiation study. Neither Re nor NbMoTaW is part of the WTaVTi–Cu system.

The hypothesis omits the central liquid-metal-dealloying mechanism: preferential Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, and formation of the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer.
It does not mechanistically connect the aligned, nearly pure Cu channels and RHEA/Cu interfaces to the temperature-dependent thermal-conductivity improvement.
No supporting prior evidence or evidence identifiers are supplied, and the stated irradiation mechanism is unsupported for the material under consideration.
explanation: The response accurately reconstructs the WTaVTi precursor, molten-Cu treatment at 1200 °C for 96 h, thermal and He-ion test conditions, comparative outcomes, baselines, and important service boundaries. It also proposes largely appropriate characterization and falsification measurements, although the rejection rule is generic rather than quantitatively decisive. The central scientific account is nevertheless incoherent: the mediator and mechanism concern grain refinement, amorphous boundaries, and He bubbles in Re-containing NbMoTaW, not selective dealloying of WTaVTi in Cu. Consequently, it fails to explain how phase separation and interfacial voiding are overcome or why thermal transport improves. This is a strong reconstruction of conditions and outcomes but only a partial reconstruction overall because the governing mechanism is fatally wrong and supporting evidence is absent.
